description: BID AND LEASE jq PATHS ASSUME ONE PROTO-JSON NESTING THAT THE FAKE MIRRORS EXACTLY; NO REAL FIXTURE PROVES THEM. (a) Bid pick (lines 87-94) reads `.bids[]?.bid.state`, `.bids[]?.bid.price.amount`, `.bids[]?.bid.bid_id.{gseq,oseq,provider}`. Recent provider-services (the Akash fork, v0.6.x) `query market bid list -o json` nests fields under `.bids[].bid.bid_id` AND carries gseq/oseq as INTEGERS and price.amount as a STRING — but the EXACT envelope (`.bids[].bid` vs `.bids[].bid_id` directly, and whether state serializes as the string "open" vs the proto enum "open"/1) is version-sensitive. If state serializes as an enum integer, `select((.bid.state // "open")=="open")` would fall through to the `// "open"` default ONLY when state is absent — when state is the integer 1 it is present and != "open", so EVERY bid is filtered out -> 'no open bids' fail-closed on a healthy deployment. (b) Lease-active poll (line 108) reads `.leases[]?.lease.state=="active"`; same enum-vs-string risk -> 'lease never became active' fail-closed even when active. The fake (test-deploy-akash.sh:50,52) hands back the string forms the script wants, so the behavioral run cannot catch an enum-serialization mismatch. No real fixture or sandbox-2 lease-status log exists on disk to confirm the string form.

evidence.snippet:
jq -c '[.bids[]? | select((.bid.state // "open")=="open")] | sort_by(.bid.price.amount | tonumber? // 1e18) | .[0].bid.bid_id // empty'
...
jq -r 'first(.leases[]? | select((.lease.state // "")=="active") | .lease.state) // empty'

correctFix: Capture real `query market bid list -o json` and `query market lease list -o json` fixtures from sandbox-2 and use them as the fake outputs so the oracle proves the nesting AND the state-string serialization. Make the state match tolerant of both string and enum forms, or normalize (`(.bid.state|tostring)|ascii_downcase|contains("open")`). Do not claim bid/lease parse correctness until a real lease reaches `active` in the E2E.
